name: Dana Torres

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal workday look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I play cello in a small touring quartet, record study excerpts for a music centre, and teach three adult beginners. I have a music bachelor’s degree and twenty years of paid playing, but most calls are short contracts. The bow feels steady in my hand; the calendar does not.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How does that schedule fit the household?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58, my children are grown, and my partner repairs bicycles for wages that change with the season. We rent and have about three weeks of expenses saved. My music pay is below the usual rate, and there are few similar posts nearby, even though I can play the work well.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the quartet that a faster booking email is fine if the paid rehearsal remains on the sheet. A machine cannot hold the long cello note with my quartet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Three weeks saved is already a poor buffer for a cancelled tour date. My partner’s winter repair hours drop, so mild AI does not settle the rent worry.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would keep the paid quartet calls, recordings and three pupils, and ask the centre for written fees and cancellation terms. In the first year of this modest change I would use an occasional AI calendar draft only after checking every paid date against the manager’s sheet; I would not buy a new tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because a cancelled fee could leave us short this winter. AI being mild does not make the old gap go away.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Has a date already vanished?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A venue cancelled one October concert after our travel was booked. We got no show fee, and I used nearly a week of savings for the rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the children cover a bill?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They have their own homes and bills. I would ask them to listen to a rehearsal, not to carry our rent.

say: I would accept **faster booking emails** with paid rehearsal fees still written down.
I would say **live quartet playing** still needs musicians in the room.
think: Our **three-week reserve** cannot absorb another unpaid cancellation.
My partner’s **winter repair hours** already make household income uneven.
do: Keep **paid quartet calls**, recordings and three pupils this season.
Request **written fees** and cancellation terms; check occasional AI calendar drafts against the manager’s sheet.
feel: I feel **anxious** about an ordinary cancellation reaching our rent.
S0.quote: A machine cannot hold the long cello note with my quartet.
fieldNote: Her **experienced cello playing** brings below-usual pay on short quartet and study contracts that can vanish between seasons.
An existing **AI calendar draft** is checked manually against paid dates, not newly learned from a tool course.

steps.text: Keep paid quartet calls, study recordings and three pupils this season
Request written fees/cancellation terms and verify AI dates against manager sheet

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the centre that generated study excerpts could undercut the recordings it buys from me. I would ask the musicians’ association to press for paid rehearsal and cancellation terms in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The excerpts bring about a third of my own pay, and there are few other music posts here. If the centre replaces them, three weeks saved will not carry a long search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would total the last six months of recording invoices and join the musicians’ association’s fee meeting. In the first year, if study orders fall, I would stop renting the spare rehearsal room on empty days and keep pupils and paid quartet calls; I would ask the centre for signed paid dates before dropping any work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about a realistic cut to my own recording income. A shared fee request might help, but no meeting pays next month’s rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the association to put forward?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I want cancellation pay and preparation hours written into each centre call. A general promise to support live music would not pay anyone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you replace recordings with extra lessons?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if adults actually book paid slots outside my quartet rehearsals. I cannot write their fees into the budget before they sign up.

say: I would warn **generated excerpts** may replace paid recordings.
I would ask the **musicians’ association** to seek written fees and cancellation pay.
think: Study excerpts bring **one-third of my pay** and have few local substitutes.
Our **three-week reserve** cannot fund a long search.
do: Total **recording invoices** and join the association fee meeting now.
Stop **empty-day room hire** if orders fall; keep paid pupils/quartet and request signed centre dates.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing a regular third of my income.
S1.quote: A general promise to support live music would not pay anyone.
fieldNote: The **collective fee request** asks the musicians’ association for concrete cancellation pay and preparation hours on each centre call.
The **room cut** triggers only after study orders fall, while quartet and pupil fees still support household rent.

steps.text: Total six months of recording invoices and join musicians association fee meeting
Stop empty-day rehearsal-room hire if study orders fall
Keep paid pupils/quartet and request signed centre dates after order cuts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the quartet that thinking AGI by 2028 could produce study excerpts before a playing robot exists. Cello-playing robots come around 2031, three years later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my study recordings to disappear in 2028, taking about a third of my own pay. With three weeks saved and few nearby seats, that loss feels large even if the live quartet stays.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would count invoices, request a signed paid quartet calendar and ask for an actual pension estimate before considering a stop at sixty. In the first year after 2028, if live calls also fall, I would apply for a posted paid music-centre tutor job only if my music degree and teaching history qualify, its written net pay after travel replaces lost fees and the bus fits; I would keep pupils and live calls until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be alarmed by the expected loss of a third of my pay. I have a search plan. Three weeks of money is not much time to replace my cello recording pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the tutor vacancy be waiting?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I need to see a current paid posting with hours and qualifications. An old advert is no job offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you stop playing at sixty?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would request an actual pension estimate before considering that. I cannot assume a birthday will cover rent.

say: I would distinguish **2028 thinking AGI** from 2031 cello-playing robots.
I would say **study recordings** could disappear before live playing does.
think: I expect to lose **one-third of my pay** from study excerpts in 2028.
Three **weeks saved** and few local seats leave little search time.
do: Count **study invoices**, request a signed paid quartet calendar and an actual pension estimate now.
Seek **posted tutor work** after 2028 live cuts if music degree/teaching qualify, written replacement net after travel and buses fit.
Keep **pupils and quartet calls** until a suitable signed offer arrives.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by an expected third of my income disappearing.
S2.quote: Three weeks of money is not much time to replace my cello recording pay.
fieldNote: The **2028 recording loss** is expected before 2031 playing robots.
A **tutor move** requires a current posting, degree/experience fit, after-travel replacement pay and signed offer.

steps.text: Count study invoices; request signed paid quartet calendar and actual pension estimate now
Seek posted tutor role after live cuts if degree/teaching qualify and bus fits
Require written after-travel net replacing losses; keep paid work until signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my three pupils that AGI by 2031 leaves time to test a small paid cello basics circle. Cello-playing robots would follow around 2034, after the study-track market changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The centre recordings may end by 2031. I know how to teach bow hold and tuning, but I will not hire a hall on a hopeful list of names.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next spring I would secure written room and hire terms at the community hall before taking deposits. I would run a four-week adult cello basics circle only if six adults prepay enough for room, my travel, teaching and preparation, with inspected loan cellos or sound instruments they own. In the first year after 2031 I would repeat it only while written hall terms hold and six paid safe places still cover room, travel, teaching and preparation; if unsafe instruments leave fewer than six, I would find replacements or defer and refund everyone, while keeping my three paid pupils.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious until the cello circle pays its own costs. Five years offers a test. My cello class cannot finance empty chairs from our rent money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks a loan cello?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The hall instrument keeper must check bridges, pegs and bows before a player uses one. If an unsafe cello has no sound replacement, that place cannot count toward six.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if only four adults pay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would refund all four and wait for another date. The quartet and my three existing pupils still need their paid slots.

say: I would suggest a **paid cello basics circle** to my three pupils.
I would say **2034 playing robots** follow the 2031 change to study tracks.
think: The **recordings may end** by 2031, but hall rent cannot come from savings.
Six **paid safe places** must cover the hall, travel and my teaching/preparation.
do: Start **cello circle** only after written hall terms and six fees cover room, travel, teaching/preparation and safe inspected or owned cellos.
Renew **circle after 2031** only with written room terms and six safe paid places covering room, travel and teaching/preparation.
Replace **unsafe places** or defer and refund everyone below six paid safe places; keep three pupils.
feel: I feel **anxious** until real fees cover the class.
S3.quote: My cello class cannot finance empty chairs from our rent money.
fieldNote: The **independent circle** needs written room terms before six fees cover the hall, her travel and teaching/preparation.
An **unsafe instrument** triggers replacement or a full refund below six paying places.

steps.text: Secure written hall terms before six adults prepay room, travel and my teaching/preparation
Inspect loan cellos; replace unsafe places or defer/refund everyone below six paid safe places
Renew after 2031 with written hall terms and six paid safe places funding room/travel/teaching/preparation
Keep three paid pupils while testing adult cello circle

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the quartet that a decade to AGI by 2036 lets us ask what retirement would actually pay. Cello-playing robots follow around 2039. A birthday alone will not settle a bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 68 I may still need quartet and pupil fees. Three weeks saved now do not make retirement affordable, and I have never seen a pension estimate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would request an actual pension estimate and save ten percent of each extra paid quartet date after rent, food and cello repairs until we reach three months of expenses. In the first year after 2036 I would keep paid calls and pupils while booked; if live pay falls, I would apply for a posted centre tutor job only if my music degree and teaching qualify, written net pay after travel replaces losses and a bus serves the shifts. I would leave current work only after a suitable signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would still be anxious about work at 68 with such a thin reserve. More warning helps me check numbers, but does not itself buy the rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if there is no extra quartet date?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: There is no ten percent from that source then. I would not take food money to make a savings target look tidy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask your children to fund retirement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, they have their own bills. I want an actual pension number and paid work I can still do.

say: I would ask what **retirement would pay** during the decade before 2036.
I would separate **2036 thinking AGI** from 2039 cello-playing robots.
think: At **68**, I may still need quartet and pupil fees.
Our **three-week reserve** does not make retirement affordable.
do: Request **pension estimate** and save 10% of extra paid quartet dates after rent/food/repairs toward three months.
Keep **paid calls and pupils** after 2036 while booked until a signed replacement offer.
Seek **posted tutor work** after live pay cuts only if degree/teaching qualify, after-travel net replaces losses and buses fit.
feel: I feel **anxious** about needing paid music at 68 with little saved.
S4.quote: A birthday alone will not settle a bill.
fieldNote: The **pension amount** is unknown; age 68 does not prove entitlement.
The **three-month goal** uses only ten percent of genuinely extra paid dates after essentials.

steps.text: Request actual pension estimate; keep paid quartet calls/pupils after 2036 while booked
Save 10% of extra paid quartet fees after rent/food/repairs toward three months
Seek posted tutor job after cuts if degree/teaching qualify and bus fits
Require written after-travel net replacing losses; keep music until signed offer

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because a third of my fee income could vanish before I can replace it. Signed quartet dates, an actual pension estimate and a posted tutor role with written net pay after travel would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask whether the adults in my beginner circle can pay before I book a hall. Six names on a list are not six fees in the account.

headlineQuote: Six names on a list are not six fees in the account.
portrait: At **58**, Dana is an experienced cellist with a music degree, grown children and about three weeks of expenses saved.
Her **below-usual pay** comes from quartet calls, study recordings and three pupils, with few similar local jobs.
She uses **AI occasionally** for dates but checks every booking against the manager’s sheet.
She tests a **paid cello circle** only after written room terms and six fully funded safe places.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove one-third of Dana’s income before a real replacement role appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Signed paid dates**, an actual pension estimate and a posted tutor job with written after-travel replacement pay would help.
